Issued to:
Port Said Gas Turbine Power Station

This document explains the steps of the monthly inspection of the industrial breathing apparatus, figure No. 8, as shown above, with the code M1. The first draft of this document was prepared by Dr. Ali Saber Mohamed, tested by Occupational Safety and Health technical supervisor Gamal Zaki Sobh, and approved by Eng. Sawsan Mohamed El-Lithy, Station Director. It was reviewed by Eng. Abdel Monem Attia El-Imam and Eng. Medhat Khater of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector, and approved by Eng. Samir Abdel Gilel, General Manager of Technical Inspection and MPIS coordinator, and approved by Accountant Mahmoud Soliman, Head of the Planning and Financial Forecasting Sector and supervisor of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector.
Issue a work order, with the site workers carrying the occupational safety and health category card
Fence off the work area and place the appropriate warning signs
Occupational safety and health equipment such as a safety helmet and safety belt, etc.
Check that all parts are clean and sound
Check the position of the shoulder strap and that it is not pressing on the shoulders, and that the full cylinder is placed safely on the backplate; if the cylinder is empty, replace it
Check that the strap moves freely inside the buckle
Check that the transparent front part of the facemask is clean, has no marks obstructing clear vision, and is free of any cracks, and loosen the head strap
If any defects are found in the previous four points, follow the maintenance instructions in the SIGMA 2 Service Manual
Check that the cylinder circular connection is clean and sound
Connect this connection tightly to the cylinder valve outlet
Check that the pressure gauge and hoses are in good condition and not bent or stretched
Check that the valve circular connection is clean and sound
Fix the demand valve to the facemask and check that the connection has entered its correct place gently and without force; turn the valve to make sure it is fixed safely
Check that the side (additional) valve is closed (i.e. the flat part on the switch is towards the face)
When using a demand valve that operates with the first breath, press the black button as mentioned earlier
Open the cylinder valve and check that it is full
Check that the facemask receives pressure; if needed, adjust the mask to prevent leakage, but do not tighten the strap more than necessary because that damages the mask
Place two fingers under the mask edge and check that air flows regularly out of the mask
Remove your fingers to let the mask return to its position
Open the additional (side) passage and check that air flows regularly to the mask
Close the cylinder valve, hold your breath, watch the pressure gauge for 10 seconds and check that the pressure reading does not drop during this period (10 sec)
While the cylinder valve is still closed, follow the pressure gauge and blow exhaled air into the apparatus and check that the whistle sounds clearly at a pressure between 50-60 bar
Remove the head strap and facemask
The apparatus that has passed all these tests is considered ready for use
Check that the valve is closed, then act slowly to undo the cylinder connection; remove the reducer (4.2) from the cylinder
Pull the cylinder band closing buckle with the index finger and thumb of the right hand, and use the left index finger to push the supported latch and push the buckle
Open the buckle and carry the empty cylinder off the backplate
Fixing a replacement cylinder of the same size
Fix the cylinder valve in its place, connect the buckle holder and close the cylinder band
Fixing a cylinder of different sizes
Adjust the cylinder strap and its length to allow connecting the buckle holder
Do not close the cam until you have checked that this length is suitable
Arrange a place for the free end of the cylinder strap so that it does not hang down

SIGMA-2 with facemask 
69 x 41 x 28 cm 5.0 kg

EN 137 Open circuit self contained 
compressed air breathing apparatus

EN 136 Full facemasks for respiratory 
protective devices

Compact positive pressure demand valve featuring servo-assisted, tilting 
diaphragm mechanism with low inspiratory resistance and responsive dynamic 
performance, instant positive pressure and hands free bypass facility. 
Components injection moulded from polyamide and acetal with rubber seals and 
diaphragms

Peak flow performance:- 
in excess of 500 liters / minute

The high pressure cylinder connector and first stage pressure reducing valve 
are integrated.
The cylinder connector features a universal 200 or 300 bar handwheel connection 
and incorporates a sintered bronze particulate filter (30-40 microns) The 
pressure reducer features a non-adjustable, spring loaded piston mechanism and 
outlet supply protected by pressure relief valve

Valve body and cap machined from nickel plated brass with stainless steel 
spring and hose retaier U-clips

Flow restrictor to gauge supply hose < 25 liters 
minute

Bourdon tube type dial indicator
Heat and impact resistant polycarbonate lens
Safety blow - out vent in rear of gauge
Photo-luminescent face
Accuracy: +/- 10 bar between 40 - 300 bar
Whistle: 55 bar

Medium pressure hose:
Maximum working pressure 16 bar
Minimum burst pressure 80 bar

High pressure hose:
Maximum working pressure 450 bar
Minimum burst pressure 800 
bar

The Sabre Panaseal positive pressure facemask is has non-dermatitic neoprene 
inner and outer mask materials, a scratch and impact resistant polycarbonate 
visor and a five point rubber headharness. The mask also features a front 
mounted speech diaphragm, with a side mounted demand valve for reduced profile 
and unimpeded speech transmission. The positive pressure exhalation valve has an 
operating pressure 4.4 and 6.0 m bar. The mask also accepts integrated spectacle 
frames with out compromising the facemask seal.

Introduction
This document explains the steps of the monthly inspection of the industrial breathing apparatus, figure No. 8, as shown above, with the code M1. The first draft of this document was prepared by Dr. Ali Saber Mohamed, tested by Occupational Safety and Health technical supervisor Gamal Zaki Sobh, and approved by Eng. Sawsan Mohamed El-Lithy, Station Director. It was reviewed by Eng. Abdel Monem Attia El-Imam and Eng. Medhat Khater of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector, and approved by Eng. Samir Abdel Gilel, General Manager of Technical Inspection and MPIS coordinator, and approved by Accountant Mahmoud Soliman, Head of the Planning and Financial Forecasting Sector and supervisor of the Inspection and Quality Control Sector.
Safety precautions
Issue a work order, with the site workers carrying the occupational safety and health category card |

Tools, instruments and equipment used

Procedures to be carried out
Before use
General instructions
Check that all parts are clean and sound | 1.
Check the position of the shoulder strap and that it is not pressing on the shoulders, and that the full cylinder is placed safely on the backplate; if the cylinder is empty, replace it | 2.
Check that the strap moves freely inside the buckle | 3.
Check that the transparent front part of the facemask is clean, has no marks obstructing clear vision, and is free of any cracks, and loosen the head strap | 4.
If any defects are found in the previous four points, follow the maintenance instructions in the SIGMA 2 Service Manual | 5.
Pneumatic devices
Figure No. 1
Check that the cylinder circular connection is clean and sound | 1.
Connect this connection tightly to the cylinder valve outlet | 2.
Check that the pressure gauge and hoses are in good condition and not bent or stretched | 3.
Demand valve
Figures No. 2, 3
Check that the valve circular connection is clean and sound | 1.
Fix the demand valve to the facemask and check that the connection has entered its correct place gently and without force; turn the valve to make sure it is fixed safely | 2.
Check that the side (additional) valve is closed (i.e. the flat part on the switch is towards the face) | 3.
When using a demand valve that operates with the first breath, press the black button as mentioned earlier | 4.
Facemask condition, see part (4.2)
Open the cylinder valve and check that it is full | 1.
Check that the facemask receives pressure; if needed, adjust the mask to prevent leakage, but do not tighten the strap more than necessary because that damages the mask | 2.
Positive pressure test
Figures No. 4, 5
Place two fingers under the mask edge and check that air flows regularly out of the mask | 1.
Remove your fingers to let the mask return to its position | 2.
Open the additional (side) passage and check that air flows regularly to the mask | 3.
Close the cylinder valve, hold your breath, watch the pressure gauge for 10 seconds and check that the pressure reading does not drop during this period (10 sec) | 4.
Whistle test
Figure No. 6
While the cylinder valve is still closed, follow the pressure gauge and blow exhaled air into the apparatus and check that the whistle sounds clearly at a pressure between 50-60 bar | 1.
Remove the head strap and facemask | 2.
The apparatus that has passed all these tests is considered ready for use | 3.
Cylinder replacement
Figure No. 7
Check that the valve is closed, then act slowly to undo the cylinder connection; remove the reducer (4.2) from the cylinder | 1.
Pull the cylinder band closing buckle with the index finger and thumb of the right hand, and use the left index finger to push the supported latch and push the buckle | 2.
Open the buckle and carry the empty cylinder off the backplate | 3.
Fixing a replacement cylinder of the same size
Fix the cylinder valve in its place, connect the buckle holder and close the cylinder band | 1.
Fixing a cylinder of different sizes
Adjust the cylinder strap and its length to allow connecting the buckle holder | 1.
Do not close the cam until you have checked that this length is suitable | 2.
Arrange a place for the free end of the cylinder strap so that it does not hang down | 3.

uncertain_terms.note: Rendered 'cylinder band' by intent (the band with the buckle that holds the cylinder); literally 'mask'.
The source omits which valve ('تأكد أن صمام مغلق'); rendered 'the valve is closed' by intent (the cylinder valve).
The black button was not mentioned earlier in this document; kept verbatim.
Source typo (double alif) for النقاط الأربعة; rendered 'the previous four points'.
Source typo for إلى ماسك الوجه; rendered 'to the facemask'.
Garbled wording in the source; rendered by intent as pushing the latch and the buckle.
Stray '000' before 'etc.' in the source; rendered 'etc.'.
Source typo for أن; rendered 'Check that all parts...'.
